name: geographr
summary: Find UK boundaries, geographical lookups and rural–urban classifications.
description: An R package for analysts working with UK geography. It provides boundary and point geometries, lookup tables and functions for common aggregation tasks.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: Check the geography codes and boundary editions before combining datasets; the README identifies the package as work in progress.

name: demographr
summary: Find population estimates to understand the people living in a UK area.
description: An R data package for analysts working with UK demographic data. Population estimate tables are distributed as data frames for use in your own analysis.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: Coverage and reference years vary by dataset. Check each table’s documentation before comparing places or time periods.

name: compositr
summary: Combine indicators into composite scores and indices in R.
description: A suite of R functions for combining and manipulating indicators. Analysts can use it to build composite scores and indices with their own data and methodological choices.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: The package is work in progress. Indicator selection, weighting and interpretation require judgment; a score does not determine humanitarian priorities.

name: humanicheck
summary: Check a dataset for missing values, duplicate rows, outliers and geometry issues.
description: Pass a data frame or tibble to humanicheck() for a readable data quality report in your R console. It checks object size, duplicates, missing values, numerical outliers and consistency of spatial geometry types.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: These diagnostics flag possible issues. They cannot establish whether a dataset is appropriate, complete or representative for your task.

name: floodvulnerability
summary: Explore neighbourhood social vulnerability to flooding across the UK.
description: Datasets from Sayers and Partners describe neighbourhood flood vulnerability and flood disadvantage. The collection also includes SEPA flood areas for Scotland.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
coverage: United Kingdom; coverage varies by dataset
limitations: The 2025 neighbourhood index is UK-wide. Flood disadvantage covers England and Wales (2022); Scottish flood areas are from 2024. Social vulnerability is not a forecast of a particular flood.
dataPeriod: Neighbourhood vulnerability: 2025; flood disadvantage: 2022; Scottish flood areas: 2024

name: Intersectional risks
summary: Inspect a prototype exploring overlapping dimensions of vulnerability.
description: A research repository prototyping an intersectional vulnerability map. It makes the code and research material available for inspection.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: The README identifies this as a prototype and does not document coverage or operational suitability. No hosted app destination is documented.

name: Vulnerability Index Builder
summary: Turn your indicator spreadsheet into a composite vulnerability index in your browser.
description: Upload Excel or CSV indicator data, group indicators into weighted domains and export scores, ranks and vulnerability bands. The browser app includes a guided wizard and a workspace, with an example dataset to try.
limitations: Prepare one row per area with matching area codes. Computation happens in your browser. Review missing values, indicator direction, weighting and sensitivity; the tool does not choose appropriate priorities for you.

name: shinycoin
summary: Build, explore and export composite indices with a guided COINr interface.
description: A locally run Shiny app wrapping COINr’s composite index methods. It includes data screening, normalisation, weighting, aggregation, visualisation and uncertainty analysis, plus a replication script.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: Requires R and the shiny, COINr, ggplot2 and plotly packages. Follow the repository’s local launch instructions; no hosted app URL is documented.

name: IMD
summary: Access deprivation indices and community needs data for all four UK nations.
description: An R package providing Indices of Multiple Deprivation at several geographical levels, Community Needs Index files and selected household deprivation figures. A released version is available on CRAN; data downloads are linked in its README.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: National deprivation indices use different methods and dates. Do not assume their scores are directly comparable. Consult the documentation for any composite UK comparisons.

name: healthyr
summary: Find UK health datasets for analysis in R.
description: An R package distributing UK health data for analysts. The repository documents installation and how the packaged datasets are maintained.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: The README marks the project as work in progress. Check the source, period and geographical coverage of each dataset.

name: asylum
summary: Access UK asylum and resettlement statistics published by the Home Office.
description: An R package for analysing Home Office asylum and resettlement datasets, with a released version available from CRAN.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: The README describes a September 2023 data release. Check the packaged data and original Home Office publications before using it to describe current conditions.
dataPeriod: September 2023 release described in the README

name: Loneliness index
summary: Explore neighbourhood loneliness indicators for the four UK nations.
description: A research project scoring and ranking neighbourhoods for loneliness. England uses a self-reported survey; Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland use prescriptions associated with loneliness-related conditions.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: Scores are comparable within nations, not between nations. Prescribing patterns are proxies and do not measure an individual’s experience of loneliness. The project is under development.

name: peralta
summary: Check whether new datasets have been published on webpages you follow.
description: An R package that checks a list of webpage URLs for updates, helping data maintainers notice when new source material appears.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: The README identifies it as work in progress. A detected webpage change still needs review to establish what changed in the underlying data.

name: wildfires
summary: Explore how wildfire risk and social vulnerability overlap across the UK.
description: An R package providing social vulnerability indicators and modelled spring and summer wildfire risk at MSOA level or national equivalents.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: Risk and vulnerability scores are standardised separately within each UK nation. They are analytical estimates, not live incident forecasts or evidence of individual vulnerability.

name: broadcast
summary: Make the datasets in an R package available as CSV files.
description: An R utility for package maintainers. It converts .rda data files into CSV files so that people can use the data outside R.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: Requires an R package containing data files. Check the underlying data’s reuse terms before publishing the exported CSVs.

name: Health Inequalities Explorer data
summary: Inspect the datasets used in the Health Inequalities Explorer.
description: A repository containing datasets used in the Health Inequalities Explorer. It provides access to the source files rather than a documented hosted explorer.
limitations: The README does not describe geographical coverage, periods or individual data definitions. Review the files and their provenance before use.

name: Compare risk maps
summary: Compare overlaps between disaster risk, resilience and vulnerability maps.
description: A Shiny app for comparing the overlaps and differences between maps, including flooding, heatwaves, deprivation and social fabric.
limitations: Check the app’s source datasets and geographical coverage. Overlapping map classifications do not establish causes or automatically identify priorities.

name: Heat disadvantage
summary: Explore heat vulnerability and disadvantage datasets for Great Britain.
description: Heat disadvantage datasets combine heat exposure and social vulnerability. England and Wales use Climate Just indices; Scotland uses 4 Earth Intelligence heat hazard and deprivation data.
limitations: Methods differ between Scotland and England/Wales, and classifications are calculated separately by nation. Northern Ireland data are not included. See the README for baseline and warming scenarios.
dataPeriod: England/Wales: 2022 Climate Just indices; baseline and 1.5°C scenarios

name: DEPAHRI
summary: Examine physical and digital barriers to accessing healthcare.
description: The Digital Exclusion and Physical Access to Healthcare Risk Index combines demography, deprivation, digital connectivity and physical access to healthcare.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: Each of four components is equally weighted. Higher scores indicate greater exclusion risk; an area score is not a measure of an individual’s access. The package’s reuse license is not yet specified.

name: specr (Humaniverse fork)
summary: Inspect how analytical choices affect statistical results using specification curves.
description: Humaniverse’s fork of the specr R package. The upstream project provides tools to set up, run and visualise specification curve analyses; its documentation is linked here.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: The upstream package documents a stable lifecycle; this fork’s maturity is not separately documented. Specification curves show sensitivity to analytical choices and do not make an estimate more valid or generalisable.

name: globalvuln
summary: Compare global vulnerability indices and access country-level data in R.
description: An R data package and browser explorer bringing together published indices of vulnerability, fragility, development, hunger, health and displacement. The explorer helps compare concepts, coverage and sources.
coverage: Global; country-level coverage varies by index
limitations: Original publisher scores retain their scales. No cross-index meta-score is produced; missing coverage must not be read as low vulnerability. Reference periods and reuse terms differ by publisher.

name: Anticipatory analysis field guide
summary: Learn and facilitate anticipatory humanitarian analysis.
description: An interactive field guide with lessons, a working session and workshop facilitation material. It is based on a method developed by Madeleine Lyons and Barbara Devlieger.
limitations: Working sessions are stored in your browser; export backups to keep your work. Fictional examples are learning material. The guide supports discussion and does not select priorities automatically.

name: Health Index for Wales
summary: Inspect work towards a health index for Welsh local authorities.
description: A work in progress project based on the Office for National Statistics Health Index, with healthy people, healthy lives and healthy places domains.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: The README says data collection was paused awaiting a new StatsWales API. A restart is not confirmed in the README; all data and outputs require careful review.

name: Deprivation Explorer
summary: Explore the UK’s indices of multiple deprivation in your browser.
description: A Shiny app for exploring the UK’s indices of multiple deprivation. Its source repository is available alongside the hosted app.
limitations: Check the edition, national methodology and geography shown in the app. Scores from separate national indices are not automatically comparable.

name: Health Index Scotland
summary: Inspect indicators and methods for a Scottish health index.
description: A work in progress project to build a Scottish Health Index using the indicators and methodology of England’s Health Index. The README includes indicator metadata and source links.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: The project is still in development. Reference years and source licenses differ by indicator; do not treat the collection as a reviewed current operational index.

name: Northern Ireland health indicators
summary: Inspect health inequality indicators collected for Northern Ireland.
description: A development repository collecting health inequality indicators. Its metadata documents topics including smoking, school attendance, alcohol misuse and cardiovascular conditions.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: The package description is unfinished and several indicators are unavailable. Consult the metadata for source years, definitions and licensing; this is not a complete, reviewed health index.

name: fermi
summary: Make probabilistic estimates by breaking a question into smaller uncertain quantities.
description: An R package for Fermi estimation. Analysts define assumptions for component quantities and use Monte Carlo simulation to examine the distribution of possible outcomes.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: Results depend on your assumptions and the way the components combine. They are estimates with uncertainty, not observed totals or forecasts guaranteed by the package.

name: shinyspecr
summary: Interactively examine specification curves and the models behind them.
description: An R package opening a Shiny explorer for a specr analysis. It includes a specification curve, model tables, distributions and summaries of analytical choices.
prerequisites: Requires an R installation and the project’s documented dependencies.
limitations: Requires R and a specr result object; supplying the original dataset enables model refitting. No hosted app destination is documented. Follow the repository’s installation instructions.
